claim.summary: Indigenous Hawaiian historical traditions and later specialist scholarship describe kauwā as a small, hereditary and strongly segregated status group within late precontact Hawaiian society. result.bounded_proposition: Around the late ninth/early tenth century, parts of the wider Viking/Rūs mobile network demonstrably engaged in capture, transport and sale of people, with near-anchor eastern evidence for explicit sale and independent western evidence for extensive captive-taking.
result.category_mapping_note: Contemporary external sources support captive/slave sale; later Old Norse thrall terminology requires source criticism; Saqaliba and Rūs are source categories, not precise modern nationalities.
result.evidence_locus_summary: Eastern river routes linking Rūs, Slavic regions, Khazar and Volga Bulgar markets; western raiding zones and ship camps; Birka/Hedeby/Dublin as archaeological node context
result.geometry_unresolved_note: No giant Viking territory; future display should use route/nodal semantics or unresolved network geometry without strengthening claims.
result.historical_terms: þræll/thrall; Saqaliba; captive/prisoner; enslaved woman/concubine; Rūs
result.inference_extent_summary: Network participation and bounded capture/sale practices only; no territorial practice or population prevalence assigned to connected regions.
result.language_access_limitations: Translated Arabic and western annal material plus specialist synthesis reviewed; Arabic originals and Old Norse manuscript traditions not independently edited.
result.law_practice_note: No single Viking legal regime governs the evidence; later Scandinavian laws illuminate thraldom but cannot substitute for c.900 mobile-network practice.
result.network_territorial_note: Primary positive dimension is network participation; route/node evidence must not be converted into a territorial Viking slavery polygon.
result.required_abstention: Do not treat the network as one polity or society; do not assume every captive was enslaved/sold, every port was a slave market, or connected territories shared one practice level; do not infer volume from dirhams/restraints.

reviews.dependency_or_scope_note: Network positive only; no homogeneous Viking polity.
reviews.notes: Gate-2 import preserves internal review only; independent historical review remains zero.
reviews.review_reason: Near-anchor evidence supports capture, transport and sale within parts of the mobile Viking/Rus network without territorial-state inference.
